steps.instruction: This is the XIAO ESP32-S3 - the tiny computer for this build. It has Wi-Fi built in.
details: Take the XIAO out of its bag and hold it by the edges.
Find the silver metal can: that's the chip with the Wi-Fi radio.
Count the gold pins: 7 on each long side.
Keep it away from metal tables and coins - the pins can short.
steps.look_for: You can point to the chip, the pins and the USB-C socket.
steps.watch_out: Hold it by the edges - fingers on the chip can carry static.

steps.instruction: Find the USB-C port, the B (boot) and R (reset) buttons and the little user LED.
details: USB-C: the metal socket on the short end.
B: the tiny button marked B - you only need it if uploading fails.
R: the button marked R restarts the board.
The user LED is the small light near the socket - it shows what the board is doing.
steps.watch_out: Press buttons gently with a fingertip, not a pen.

steps.instruction: Connect the board to your computer with a USB-C DATA cable.
details: Plug the small USB-C end into the XIAO.
Plug the other end into a laptop or desktop with Chrome or Edge.
Some cables only charge - if nothing happens in the next step, try another cable.
steps.watch_out: Use Chrome or Edge on a computer - phones and Safari can't flash boards.

stages.title: Put the brain on the board

steps.instruction: Open the Tender Cells browser flasher and pick the Starter Node.
details: Open tendercells.com/flash in Chrome or Edge.
Choose a Starter Node card, such as 'Open/close a door' or 'Lamp / pump / fan'.
Click Connect / Install, then choose the port that appeared when you plugged in.
Click Install and wait until it says done (about a minute). Don't unplug while it runs.
steps.look_for: The flasher says the install is complete.
steps.watch_out: Port missing? Try another DATA cable, or hold B, tap R, release B, and try again.

steps.instruction: The board restarts by itself after flashing; its LED starts blinking quickly (setup mode).
details: Wait a few seconds after the install finishes.
Look at the user LED: a fast blink means it's waiting to be set up.
Nothing at all? Press R once to restart it.
steps.watch_out: Keep the cable plugged in: the board needs power for the next steps.

steps.instruction: On a phone or laptop, join the Wi-Fi network called TenderNode-Setup.
details: Open Wi-Fi settings on a phone or laptop.
Pick TenderNode-Setup from the list (it has no password).
A setup page opens by itself. If it doesn't, open a browser and go to 192.168.4.1.
steps.watch_out: This network only exists while the board is in setup mode - if it's missing, press R on the board.

steps.instruction: Choose your home Wi-Fi (2.4 GHz) and type its password.
details: Tap Configure WiFi on the setup page.
Pick your home network from the list.
Type the Wi-Fi password carefully (letters are case-sensitive).
Ask the owner of the Wi-Fi before using it. Never use a school or office password.
steps.look_for: Your network name and password are filled in.
steps.watch_out: ESP32 boards can't see 5 GHz networks. If yours only shows '-5G', use the 2.4 GHz one.

steps.instruction: Fill in Broker IP, Broker port 1883, Device ID and Product type, then Save.
details: Broker IP: the address your Tender Cells hub printed when it started (e.g. 192.168.1.50). Leave it blank to let the board search.
Broker port: 1883.
Device ID: keep the suggested node_XXXX, or give it a name.
Product type: chicken-tender (or starter, duck-dock, …).
Tap Save. The setup network disappears - that's expected.
steps.look_for: The page says it saved and TenderNode-Setup goes away.
steps.watch_out: Typo in the broker IP? The board won't appear. Press R and run setup again.

steps.instruction: Watch the user LED: a slow blink (½ s on, ½ s off) means it joined Wi-Fi and the broker.
details: Look at the user LED for about 20 seconds.
Slow, steady blink = online and sending a heartbeat every 10 seconds.
Fast blink again = it couldn't join; check the Wi-Fi password and broker IP.
steps.watch_out: Make sure your hub is running (npm run dev or npm run demo) before you expect it to connect.

steps.instruction: Open the Tender Cells dashboard and find your node_XXXX.
details: Open the Tender Cells OS and go to Dashboard.
Look in the device list for your Device ID (node_XXXX or the name you chose).
Open it: its heartbeat arrives on tc/{id}/sensors every 10 seconds.
steps.look_for: Your node is listed and online. You built a live device!
steps.watch_out: Not there after a minute? Check the hub is running on the same network and the broker IP matches.
